questions.question: Identify the ‘last-living’ Sadir dancer who received the Padma Shri in 2022.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is R Muthukannammal.

  • R Muthukannammal is recognized as the 'last-living' Sadir dancer.
  • She was awarded the Padma Shri in 2022 for her contributions to the art form.
  • Sadir is the traditional name for Bharatanatyam, a classical Indian dance form.

Additional Information

  • Padma Shri
    • The Padma Shri is the fourth highest civilian award in the Republic of India.

    • The awards are announced every year on the occasion of Republic Day.

    • Sadir, also known as Sadir Natyam, is the traditional name for what is now known as Bharatanatyam.
    • It originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu and was traditionally performed by Devadasis.
    • The dance form is known for its grace, purity, tenderness, and sculpturesque poses.
    • R Muthukannammal, being the last-living practitioner, has played a crucial role in keeping this ancient dance form alive.
  • Bharatanatyam
    • Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India.
    • It is characterized by intricate footwork, expressive hand gestures, and elaborate costumes.
    • The dance form has its origins in Tamil Nadu and is known for its storytelling through dance.

questions.question: Which of the following awards was conferred on Krishna Sobti in the year 1980 for her Hindi novel ‘Zindaginama’?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following awards was conferred on Krishna Sobti in the year 1980 for her Hindi novel ‘Zindaginama’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sahitya Akademi Award.

Key Points

  • Krishna Sobti was an Indian Hindi-language fiction writer and essayist.
  • She won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1980 for her novel Zindaginama and in 1996, was awarded the Sahitya Akademi Fellowship.
  • She also received the Jnanpith Award for her contribution to Indian literature.
  • Her publications have been translated into multiple Indian and foreign languages such as Swedish, Russian and English.
  • Krishna Sobti is best known for her 1966 novel Mitro Marajani, an unapologetic portrayal of a married woman's sexuality.
  • Krishna Sobti was also the recipient of the first Katha Chudamani Award, in 1999, for Lifetime Literary Achievement, apart from winning the Shiromani Award in 1981, Hindi Academy Award in 1982, Shalaka Award of the Hindi Academy Delhi, and in 2008, her novel Samay Sargam was selected for Vyas Samman, instituted by the K. K. Birla Foundation.

Additional Information

  • The Sahitya Akademi Award is a literary honour in India, which the Sahitya Akademi, India's National Academy of Letters, annually confers on writers of the most outstanding books of literary merit published in any of the 24 major Indian languages.
  • The Saraswati Samman is an annual award for outstanding prose or poetry literary works in any of the 22 languages of India listed in Schedule VIII of the Constitution of India. It is named after an Indian goddess of knowledge.
  • The Jnanpith Award is the oldest and the highest Indian literary award presented annually by the Bharatiya Jnanpith to an author for their "outstanding contribution towards literature.
  • The Vyas Samman is a literary award in India, first awarded in 1991. It is awarded annually by the K.K. Birla Foundation and includes a cash payout of Rs 4,00,000.

questions.question: Pt. Bhimsen Joshi has received highest civilian award Bharat Ratna in which of the following year?
questions.questionHtml: Pt. Bhimsen Joshi has received highest civilian award Bharat Ratna in which of the following year?
questions.solution: Pt. Bhimsen Joshi received the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 2009 for his exceptional contributions to Hindustani classical music. Instituted in 1954, the Bharat Ratna recognizes exceptional service without distinction of race, occupation, position, or sex. Recipients receive a certificate signed by the President of India and a medallion. Initially limited to arts, literature, science, and public services, the award's criteria were expanded in 2011 to include any field of human endeavor. Notable recipients include Mother Teresa, Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, Sachin Tendulkar, and Nelson Mandela, with 48 individuals honored as of 2023.

questions.question: Kalaguru Bishnu Rabha Award is given by which government in the field of dance and music?
questions.questionHtml: Kalaguru Bishnu Rabha Award is given by which government in the field of dance and music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Assam.

  • The Kalaguru Bishnu Rabha Award is given by the Government of Assam to recognize exceptional contributions in the field of dance and music.
  • This award is named after Bishnu Prasad Rabha, a renowned cultural icon, artist, and revolutionary leader of Assam.
  • It honors individuals who have significantly promoted and preserved the rich cultural heritage of Assam.
  • The award is presented annually during Bishnu Rabha Divas, observed on June 20th to commemorate the death anniversary of Bishnu Rabha.
  • Recipients are recognized for their outstanding achievements in Assamese art, music, dance, and literature.

Additional Information

  • Bishnu Prasad Rabha
    • He was an influential figure in Assamese culture, known as "Kalaguru" for his exceptional contributions to art and music.
    • Rabha was also a freedom fighter, poet, and social reformer who advocated for the upliftment of marginalized communities.
    • His works reflect themes of patriotism, social justice, and cultural preservation.
  • Significance of Cultural Awards
    • Cultural awards like the Kalaguru Bishnu Rabha Award help promote and preserve regional art forms.
    • They encourage younger generations to engage in traditional music, dance, and literature.
    • Such awards play a crucial role in sustaining the cultural identity of a region.
  • Other Awards in Assam
    • Srimanta Sankardev Award: Recognizes contributions in art, culture, and philosophy.
    • Assam Ratna Award: Given for exceptional contributions in various fields.
    • These awards reflect Assam’s rich cultural legacy and commitment to honoring its heritage.
  • Dance and Music in Assam
    • Assam is known for its vibrant dance forms like Bihu, Sattriya, and Bagurumba.
    • Traditional music forms include Bihu Geet, Zikir, and Goalpariya Lokgeet.
    • These art forms are integral to Assamese identity and are celebrated globally.

questions.question: Harivarasanam award is given in the field of music by which of the following state governments?
questions.questionHtml: Harivarasanam award is given in the field of music by which of the following state governments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kerala.

Key Points

  • The Harivarasanam Award is given annually by the Kerala state government to honor individuals for their contributions to the field of music.
  • The award is named after the famous song "Harivarasanam," which is dedicated to the deity Ayyappa and is sung at the Sabarimala Temple in Kerala.
  • This award recognizes the achievements and contributions of musicians who have made significant impact in the realm of devotional and classical music.
  • The award includes a cash prize, citation, and a plaque, which are presented to the recipient during a ceremony organized by the Kerala government.

Additional Information

  • Harivarasanam
    • Harivarasanam is a Sanskrit devotional song dedicated to Lord Ayyappa.
    • It is also known as the "Lullaby Song" because it is sung just before the temple closes for the night.
    • The song describes the glory and virtues of Lord Ayyappa, and is an integral part of the rituals at the Sabarimala Temple.
    • The song was composed by Kambangudi Kulathur Srinivasa Iyer and was popularized by the renowned singer K.J. Yesudas.
  • Sabarimala Temple
    • Sabarimala Temple is one of the most famous pilgrimage centers in India, located in the Pathanamthitta district of Kerala.
    • The temple is dedicated to Lord Ayyappa, and it attracts millions of devotees every year, especially during the Mandala season (mid-November to mid-January).
    • Sabarimala is known for its unique customs, including the strict 41-day vratham (fasting and abstinence) that devotees must observe before visiting the temple.
    • The temple is situated amidst dense forests and mountains, symbolizing the spiritual journey and the ultimate union with the divine.
  • Devotional Music
    • Devotional music plays a significant role in the cultural and spiritual life of India.
    • It encompasses a wide range of genres including bhajans, kirtans, qawwalis, and more, each associated with different religious and spiritual traditions.
    • Devotional music is often performed in temples, religious ceremonies, and spiritual gatherings, serving as a medium for expressing devotion and reverence towards the divine.
    • Many renowned musicians and composers have contributed to the rich tradition of devotional music in India, making it an integral part of the country's cultural heritage.
